title: Smooth algebras over normal domains admit Noetherian normal base models in a filtered colimit
statement: Let $R$ be an integrally closed integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $S$ be a commutative ring, and let $f:R\to S$ be smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. There exist a small filtered category $I$, a diagram $F:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ with a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and a ring isomorphism $\operatorname{colim} F\cong S$, such that for every $i\in I$ there is a Noetherian commutative ring $A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], together with a smooth ring map $g_i:A_i\to F(i)$. Here normal means every prime localization is an integrally closed domain; no normality of $F(i)$ or $S$ is part of the conclusion. When $R$ and $S$ have universes $u,v$, the index and all the models can be chosen in universe $\max(u,v)$.

proof.text: Descend the smooth map to a smooth algebra $S_0$ over a finitely generated subring $R_0$ of $R$, with $S \cong R \otimes_{R_0} S_0$, by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-finite-type-model].

source.place: Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up), third paragraph; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/033C

proof.text: For each finitely generated subring $C$ containing $R_0$, normalize $C$ in its own fraction field. The normalization is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal]. The inclusion into the fraction field of $R$ identifies it with a subring of $R$: its elements are integral over $C$, hence integral over $R$, and therefore lie in the integrally closed domain $R$. The normalization is finite over $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-domain-normalization-finite]. It is consequently finite type over $\mathbf Z$, and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Its prime localizations are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain].

source.place: Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up), third paragraph; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/033C

proof.text: Let $I$ be the poset of finitely generated normal subrings $A$ of $R$ containing $R_0$. Normalizing $R_0$ proves nonemptiness; normalizing the subring generated by two members proves directedness. Every $x \in R$ belongs to a member by normalizing $R_0[x]$. Thus their union is $R$. Regard this nonempty directed poset as a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up), third paragraph; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/033C

proof.text: Set $F(A)=A\otimes_{R_0}S_0$, with transition maps induced by the inclusions of subrings. The structure map from $A$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Elements of $S$ lift to stages, and a stage element becoming zero vanishes at a later stage, by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise]. Apply this lemma to the diagram of $R_0$-algebras, rather than tensoring over a distinguished index. The inclusions of the $A$ have colimit $R$: compatible maps descend on elements of the union and preserve ring operations after moving finitely many elements to a common stage. The same elementwise construction on the base changes gives a colimit cocone with vertex $S$, and hence a ring equivalence from the categorical colimit to $S$. Apply universe lifts to the index category and the rings as necessary; the maximum of the universes of $R$ and $S$ suffices. Each stage carries its displayed smooth map from the Noetherian normal base $A$. No normality assertion about any $F(A)$ or about $S$ is used.

lean.statement: theorem exists_noetherian_normal_model_colimit {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsDomain R] [IsIntegrallyClosed R] {f : R →+* S} (hf : f.Smooth) : ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I) (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{max u v}) (_ : HasColimit F), Nonempty ((colimit F : CommRingCat.{max u v}) ≃+* S) ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ (A : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsNoetherianRing A) (g : A →+* F.obj i), g.Smooth ∧ ∀ (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime], IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)
